finding: Matches 14130 and 14164 are counted in the '13 suspected reduced overs / DLS' figure and made ineligible for that reason, but the data shows a dropped ball, not a shortened match. 14130 (LSG v MI, 2022-04-24) has over 14 with 5 legal balls in BOTH innings (119 legal each, 6/8 wickets, 20 overs bowled); 14164 (SRH v PBKS) has over 14 with 5 legal balls in innings 1. Totals/targets are probably short by the missing ball (target 168 and 157 in the data). The 'both innings ended on the same legal-ball count (119): consistent with both sides limited to the same shortened overs' evidence text is misleading. The same matches are also flagged OVER_WITH_5_LEGAL_BALLS, and the two flags are not reconciled. The result for 14130 is UNDETERMINED although a 36-run LSG win is probable.

The match results from memory (LSG 168/6, MI 132/8; SRH 157/8) are NOT verified here.
suggested_fix: Add a separate flag class MISSING_BALL_IN_SOURCE and remove these two from the 'reduced overs/DLS' count (11 not 13). Keep them ineligible, because the target and balls_left are off by one, but state the true reason. Check the official scorecards.

finding: A raw-data defect is not caught by the audit: match 20182 innings 1, over 12 ball 3 (innings_ball_num 70) lists Bhanuka Rajapaksa (id 2003) as non-striker although he was dismissed (Caught) on ball 67; the next ball again shows Jitesh Sharma. finding: Retired-not-out reading rests on inference and has a fragile 'all out' rule. 5 non-wicket rows carrying dismissed_player_id are read as retired hurt (14114, 20188, 20243, 40725, 40763); the Data Notes say 'confirm externally' but no external check is recorded. is_wicket stays false, so wickets_before does not reflect the absent batter for the rest of the innings. The result logic treats an innings as complete only at >=10 wickets or 120 legal balls, so a team all out at 9 wickets plus one retired-hurt batter would be classed as 'reduced overs/UNDETERMINED'. No such case exists in the current data.
evidence: matches_ipl.csv retired_not_out_inns1/2 > 0: 14114, 20188, 20243, 40725, 40763, all eligible and none short. Code run: eligible innings with legal<120 and wickets<10 and target not reached = 0.
suggested_fix: Verify the 5 rows against scorecards. Add a retired_absent_batters_before column so the win-probability model can use wickets-in-hand = 10 - wickets - absent. Define 'all out' as wickets + unreturned retired >= 10.

finding: 'extras_2_runs' handling is plausible but is stated as 'confirmed' on thin evidence. The only test is that 2 of 186 successful chases end on the target ball only if extras_2 is added (184 vs 186 exact; 3 balls after target without it). 'Not charged to the bowler' is an assumption (the audit table says assumed; DEFINITIONS does not). The values 1 and 4 are read as byes/leg-byes, while the ball's 'stroke' is a real shot on 17 of 20 balls (for example Cover Drive, Square Cut, Pull), as it is on ordinary bye balls, so this does not decide the question. is_four/is_six are false on all 20, which supports 'not bat runs'. Effect: 47 runs in total across the 20 balls (11 balls of 1, 9 balls of 4), so small.
evidence: step0_extras_decoding.csv rows 70-78 (section D) and 66-69; code run: ball table filtered extras_2_runs>0 (20 balls: Overstep 13, other 7; runs 0 on all).
suggested_fix: Reword DEFINITIONS to 'supported by 2 chases; not-charged-to-bowler is an assumption'. Log the assumption in DECISIONS. Report the 20 balls in the Step 3 sensitivity note.

finding: Eligibility treats four same-length shortened matches as unusable although both innings share one overs limit and no DLS revision is involved (31278 KKR v MI 16 overs, 40727 RCB v PBKS 14 overs, 50137 RR v MI 11 overs, 50371 LSG v RCB 19 overs). finding: Tie handling is undocumented in the Data Notes and DECISIONS: for the two super-over ties the match winner is the super-over winner (matches_ipl.winner) but the win-probability label is 0.5 (wp_eligibility.csv), and margin_type is 'super_over_runs' (value 2 and 3). Downstream step1b builds margin_runs only where margin_type == 'runs', so a tie decided by super over is never a 'close game' (fillna(99) > 10).
evidence: src/step0_finalize.py label rule; src/step1b_pressure.py lines 44-45 and 149; matches_ipl rows 40725, 50359.
suggested_fix: Log the 0.5 label rule in Data Notes/DEFINITIONS. Decide whether ties count as close games and, if so, set the margin to 0 for the close-game test.

finding: Independence of the gate checks is limited. (a) The audit reconciles the match table to data/work/ipl_match_keys.csv, which a different script derives with the same rules (IPL id set, first-ball date, ordering), so 'identical' proves little. (b) src/gates/step0_supervisor_check.py builds 'independent' legal-ball counts from the same hypothesis (wide, Overstep, other illegal) and the same team-id set; its independent part is the four season totals. (c) The playoff check in step0_finalize.py compares with facts rows two of which were labelled 'by position in our keys' (31289, 31291), i.e. derived from the same ordering. The audit's own structural playoff test (Q2 shares one team with Q1 and with Eliminator; Final teams come from Q1/Q2) passes in all 5 seasons and is the strong evidence.
evidence: src/step0_audit.py reconciliation block; src/gates/step0_supervisor_check.py; data/work/facts/results_verification.csv rows 31289, 31291 ('by position in our keys').
suggested_fix: State in the checkpoint that these three checks are consistency checks, not independent verification. Verify the 2023 and 2024 playoff results and dates against an official source when the hosts are allowed.
